paper_title: APEX: AFS-based Permutation family for Efficiency and eXtensibility (feat. the APEX Suite)
statement: Table A1 A partial list of the best integral distinguishers for the APEX permutation family. ? denotes a possibly nonbalanced 32-bit word, B means that all 32 bits are balanced, and b means that some of the 32 bits are balanced. A superscript denotes consecutive repetitions of the corresponding 32-bit-word symbol. One APEX-b step for b ≥ 128 comprises an AFS-64 layer (four rounds) and the linear layer; one APEX-64 step is one AFS-64 application.
